key_insight: Gas-surface scattering can change the incoming molecular population enough to reverse or reshape predicted drag, lift, shear, and heat-transfer trends in rarefied hypersonic flow.
engineering_relevance: For hypersonic vehicle and inlet design, wall accommodation models must be evaluated with population feedback, not just fixed-incidence assumptions, because macroscopic loads can change substantially across rarefied regimes.
method: Direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) for hypersonic flow over a 40° inclined flat plate.
Compared Maxwell and Cercignani-Lampis-Lord (CLL) scattering using fixed-incidence moment references and alternative-kernel re-evaluation on recorded incident populations.
Studied four benchmark conditions spanning 0.023 ≤ Kn∞ ≤ 8.439.
evidence_signal: At Kn∞=0.023, Maxwell shear and heat transfer deviated by up to 40% of diffuse-reference values, and at Kn∞=8.439 the common-incidence energy constraint still left a 3.1% heat-transfer defect.
watch_item: Agreement in selected force/heat metrics does not prove common incidence or free-molecular behavior; population feedback can hide or reverse the wall-law response.
paper_title: Gas-surface scattering and collisional feedback in rarefied hypersonic flow past an inclined flat plate
